questions: Do slalom line_loss_events fall clearly below 1.0, and does slalom max_error drop below 0.06 m?
Does the slalom finish in any trials, and at what completion_time?
Does s-bend steering_oscillation stay below about 0.35 with the wider span, or does it rise as it did in iteration 1?
Did the oval and s-bend finish rates hold at iteration 4 levels (oval 20/20, s-bend 17/20)?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 without a slalom gain, return the span to +/-0.03 m with 0.01 m pitch and try lead 0.07 m, since lead 0.04 m was clearly worse and a longer lead has not been tested. If slalom line loss falls but no trial finishes, report max_error at exit so the next step can be chosen from the reach data.

intent: Keep the iteration 4 drivetrain (wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m), body, mass, lead (0.06 m) and 12 mm footprints. Widen the seven-sensor span from +/-0.03 m to +/-0.036 m at a 0.012 m pitch, so the outer sensors reach about 0.054 m from centre. The Integrator should scale the weights to +/-2 across the new span. The steering slope falls from about 67/m to about 56/m, so kp may need to rise by roughly 20 percent to hold the same steering gain. This is a geometry-only change to test whether slalom reach is the limit.
learning: Iterations 1 to 4 show the slalom failing at max_error 0.062 to 0.064 under every sensing and track variant tried. Off-track failure is set by the 0.06 m limit, which body width cannot change, so the test now is whether the sensor reach limits the line lock.
rationale: Iteration 4 (lead 0.06 m, 12 mm footprints, +/-0.03 m span, wheel_track 0.10 m) scored 629.5, close to the best 631.8. The oval finished 20/20 in 1.82 s, so the 0.10 m track does not hurt the oval and the time margin is intact. The s-bend finished 17/20 with steering_oscillation 0.319, below the 0.35 jitter threshold. The slalom is still 0/20. Its line_loss_events are 1.0 (not below 1.0) and its max_error is 0.0619, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. That limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 m for every allowed body_width, so body width cannot help. Across all five iterations, the slalom has failed at max_error 0.062 to 0.064 whatever the lead, footprint or track. The likely cause is reach: with a 12 mm footprint and the outermost sensor at 0.03 m, the array sees the tape only to about 0.048 m from centre, so the robot loses the line before it reaches the 0.06 m limit. Lead 0.04 m hurt every track, so lead stays at 0.06 m. The 16 mm footprint gave no slalom gain. I therefore change only the span: widen it from +/-0.03 m to +/-0.036 m with seven 12 mm sensors at a 0.012 m pitch. Adjacent footprints then just abut, so the tape is still covered everywhere in the array. The line is visible out to about 0.054 m from centre, which should cut slalom line loss before the limit. wheel_track stays at 0.10 m, which the oval shows is safe. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events fall clearly below 1.0 and max_error drops toward 0.055 to 0.06, with the first slalom finishes possible. Risk: the wider span raised s-bend jitter in iteration 1 (0.25 to 0.34), so the next race must show whether steering_oscillation stays below about 0.35.
